title: Smart Pointers: Tidy Up Memory
summary: Some objects need a place in memory while your program runs. A smart pointer helps look after that place and cleans it up when it is no longer needed.
introduction: Some objects need a place in memory while your program runs. A smart pointer helps look after that place and cleans it up when it is no longer needed. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Make an object with one owner
Pass ownership to another smart pointer
Explain when an owned object is removed

blocks.text: A unique_ptr owns one object. make_unique creates it. The object is removed when its owner leaves the block.

blocks.title: smart-pointers.cpp

blocks.text: std::move lets C++ move from first. Making second from that value transfers ownership. The old pointer becomes empty. Check it before you use it.

blocks.title: smart-pointers.cpp

blocks.text: A shared_ptr lets several owners share an object. The object is removed after the last owner lets go. Prefer unique_ptr when one owner is enough.

blocks.title: smart-pointers.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: Do not call delete on an object owned by a smart pointer. The smart pointer will do that job. Also avoid shared_ptr links that keep each other alive.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change 8 to 12 in the first program. Explain why no delete line is needed.
